source.basis: Operator location page, structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading: EdgeConneX San Diego, internally coded SDG01 per the operator own market page, is a 9,477 total square foot facility with 2,386 square feet of raised floor space in San Diego, California. No overall megawatt capacity figure, opening year, or named tenant is disclosed for the facility on EdgeConneX own site. The one network-partnership announcement found for this location is a press release describing an expanded relationship with Telia Carrier aimed at improving network reach and end-user experience in the San Diego market, which names a connectivity partner rather than an anchor tenant. EdgeConneX is a US-based edge and build-to-suit data center operator founded in 2009 and headquartered in Herndon, Virginia, with regional headquarters in Amsterdam and Singapore. The company was acquired by EQT Infrastructure in 2020, and its board also includes a representative of Sixth Street, an investment firm, alongside EQT partners, though exact ownership percentages are not disclosed publicly. EdgeConneX describes its footprint today as more than 90 data centers across more than 60 markets in over 20 countries on four continents, and it operates a joint venture called AdaniConneX in India alongside a strategic investment in the China-based operator Chayora. The company model centers on build-to-suit and build-to-density facilities, ranging from small edge deployments like this San Diego site to very large campuses elsewhere in its portfolio, typically serving cloud, AI and high-performance computing, content-delivery, and network or ISP tenants, though specific named tenants are rarely disclosed publicly, consistent with the lack of tenant information found for this record. San Diego smaller facility footprint relative to EdgeConneX larger hyperscale-oriented campuses elsewhere in its portfolio is consistent with the company original edge-computing model, which emphasized smaller, regionally distributed facilities close to end users before the company later expanded into much larger build-to-suit campuses for cloud and AI customers.
profile.research_note: 9,477 sqft total / 2,386 sqft raised floor and SDG01 designation confirmed via EdgeConneX own San Diego market page. No MW, year-opened, or tenant disclosed.

reading.body:
EdgeConneX San Diego publishes 9,477 square feet of technical space but no power capacity in megawatts, making it impossible to assess its role in AI infrastructure from the published record.

The absence of a megawatt figure is the norm rather than the exception in California data center reporting. Only five of over 100 mapped facilities in the state publish power capacity at all, and those five account for 170 MW combined. This facility's small footprint and lack of disclosed load means it could serve enterprise colocation, edge content delivery, or specialized workloads, but nothing in the operator's published specifications indicates which. The certifications, ENERGY STAR, SOC 2 Type 2, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, and ISO 27001, establish that the facility meets compliance requirements for financial services and healthcare, but compliance eligibility says nothing about actual occupancy or workload type.

San Diego hosts defense, biotech, and research activity, and the facility sits 10 miles from downtown and 12 miles from the airport. The operator does not connect these industries to this campus in its public materials. Without disclosed power capacity, square footage tells almost nothing about compute density or AI relevance. The data confirms the facility exists and meets certain standards. It does not establish whether it matters to AI scaling or, conversely, why capacity figures remain unpublished across the majority of California's data center footprint.
